meaning: Someone says your computer has a problem and offers to fix it. Then they ask for money or control of your computer.
clues: A stranger says they work for a well-known computer company.
A call or pop-up says your computer has a virus or another problem.
They ask you to pay for a fix, or to let them control your computer from far away.
Real tech companies do not call out of the blue to say your computer has a problem.
It has three words. They start with T, S, and S.
assumes: A romance scam starts with a fake loving friend
A prize scam says you won a contest

decoys.meaning: A crook pretends to be a loving partner online. After gaining trust, they ask for money.
You are told you won a contest, but you must pay a fee or share private details to collect.
Someone uses your name or account numbers without your permission, such as to buy things in your name.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: If a pop-up says your computer is infected and gives a phone number, do not call. Close it. Real companies do not work that way.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Back in my day, we only let the repairman in after we called him first. That rule still holds.

sources.name: FTC, How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams

blank.sentence: A stranger said my computer had a problem and offered to fix it, then asked for money. That was a ___.

why: A stranger offers a fix, then asks for money or control of your computer.
short: Fake computer help that wants money
